questions.expectedAnswer: A step-by-step set of instructions to solve a problem or complete a task
questions.markingGuide: The correct answer is 'A step-by-step set of instructions to solve a problem or complete a task'. An algorithm is a clear, ordered sequence of steps that can be followed to achieve a specific outcome. Algorithms are used in everyday life (e.g. a recipe) as well as in computing.

questions.text: What is the binary number 1010 in decimal (base 10)?
questions.markingGuide: The correct answer is 10. In binary, each digit represents a power of 2 from right to left: 1010 = (1×8) + (0×4) + (1×2) + (0×1) = 8 + 0 + 2 + 0 = 10.

questions.text: Explain the difference between hardware and software. Give one example of each.
questions.markingGuide: 1 mark for explaining the difference: Hardware is the physical components of a computer that you can touch (tangible), while software is the programs and instructions that tell the hardware what to do (intangible). 1 mark for giving one valid example of each. Hardware examples: keyboard, mouse, monitor, CPU, hard drive, RAM, printer. Software examples: Microsoft Word, Google Chrome, Windows, macOS, Scratch, Python.

questions.text: Which of the following is the strongest password?
questions.markingGuide: The correct answer is 'Tr0pic@lFish42!'. A strong password uses a mix of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters. It should be long (at least 12 characters) and not contain common words or personal information. The other options are weak because they use common words, simple sequences, or lack variety in character types.

questions.text: Explain TWO things you should consider about your digital footprint when posting on social media.
questions.markingGuide: 1 mark for each valid consideration (2 required). Possible answers: Permanence — once something is posted online, it can be very difficult to remove completely, even if you delete it (others may have screenshotted or shared it); Future impact — potential employers, universities, and scholarships may look at your social media, so inappropriate posts could affect your future opportunities; Privacy — sharing personal information (location, school, full name) can make you vulnerable to identity theft, stalking, or scams; Audience — what you post can be seen by a wider audience than you intend, including strangers; Impact on others — posts about other people (photos, comments) should respect their privacy and consent; Reputation — your online presence contributes to how others perceive you.

questions.text: In a spreadsheet application, what character must a formula start with?
questions.markingGuide: The correct answer is '='. In spreadsheet applications such as Google Sheets or Microsoft Excel, all formulas must begin with an equals sign (=). For example, =A1+B1 adds the values in cells A1 and B1.

questions.text: Describe what debugging means in programming and explain ONE strategy for finding errors in code.
questions.markingGuide: 1 mark for describing debugging: Debugging is the process of finding and fixing errors (bugs) in a computer program that prevent it from working correctly. 1 mark for explaining a valid strategy: Trace through the code line by line to see where it stops working as expected; use print statements to display variable values at different points in the program; read error messages carefully as they often tell you the line number and type of error; test small sections of code separately to isolate the problem; use a rubber duck method — explain the code out loud step by step to identify where the logic breaks down; compare the code against the original plan or algorithm.

questions.text: A local sports club wants a simple website. Describe THREE features the website should have and explain why each would be useful for the club.
questions.markingGuide: 1 mark for each feature with a clear explanation of its usefulness (3 required). Possible features: A home page with information about the club (location, training times, contact details) — useful because new members can quickly find out how to join and where to go; A fixtures/results page — useful because members and supporters can check upcoming games and see how the team is performing; A contact or sign-up form — useful because people can register interest or ask questions without needing to visit in person; A photo/video gallery — useful because it builds community spirit and can be shared on social media to attract new members; A news or events section — useful because the club can announce upcoming tournaments, fundraisers, or social events; A members-only section — useful for sharing team sheets, training plans, or private club communications. Each feature must be distinct, clearly described, and have a specific reason why it benefits the club.
